les: Om die punt van Afrika, en 'n ontmoeting by Mosselbaai
kaps_punt: Europese handelsroete na die Ooste via Suider-Afrika; Die reis van Dias; Dias en sy bemanning ontmoet die Khoikhoi in Mosselbaai -1488

items.bewering: Speserye soos peper en kaneel het 'n baie lang pad uit die Ooste na Europa gereis.
items.blok: Hoekom Portugal 'n nuwe pad gesoek het
items.bron: Encyclopedia.com, 'Long-Distance Trade' (spice routes to Chinese and Indian markets ran across Arab- and Turkish-controlled lands, with Venetians the main European carriers; pepper especially prized); O'Rourke & Williamson, 'Did Vasco da Gama Matter for European Markets?', NBER Working Paper 11884 (2005), on Euro-Asian spice price gaps.

items.bewering: Elke handelaar op daardie pad het iets bygevoeg en die prys het al hoër geword.
items.blok: Hoekom Portugal 'n nuwe pad gesoek het
items.bron: George Mason University OLLI lecture handout ('How a Few Simple Things Changed History', class 3): a kilo of pepper costing 1-2 g of silver where it was grown cost 10-14 g at Alexandria, 14-18 g at Venice and 20-30 g in Western Europe; tolls, duties and margins added at each leg. NBER WP 11884 discusses the same price gaps. Frederic Lane's well-known dispute concerns whether prices rose OVER TIME before the 1490s, not price rises ALONG THE ROUTE, so it does not bear on this sentence.

items.bewering: Portugal wou 'n handelsroete hê waarop sy eie skepe die goedere self kon gaan haal.
items.blok: Hoekom Portugal 'n nuwe pad gesoek het
items.bron: NBER WP 11884 (O'Rourke & Williamson 2005), p. 1: da Gama, sailing east around Africa, was 'looking for better access to Asian spice supplies'; Encyclopedia.com 'Long-Distance Trade' (the Portuguese hoped to sail around Africa to the Indian Ocean, bypassing the Mediterranean intermediaries).

items.bewering: Die plan was om suid te vaar langs die weskus van Afrika. 'n Skip moes dan om die suidpunt na die Ooste draai.
items.blok: Hoekom Portugal 'n nuwe pad gesoek het
items.bron: T.A.J. Maas, 'Shifting frameworks for understanding otherness' (PhD thesis, University of Amsterdam, 2020), ch. 1 pp. 18-19, quoting Barros: the king believed that if his ships 'followed the coast which they were now discovering' they would reach the end of that land; Encyclopedia.com 'Long-Distance Trade'.

items.bewering: Die koning van Portugal het die ontdekkingsreisiger Bartolomeu Dias met 'n klein vloot suid gestuur.
items.blok: Dias vaar suid met 'n klein vloot
items.bron: South African History Online, 'Bartolomeu Dias' (King João II financed the expedition; a squadron of three ships); Wikipedia, 'Bartolomeu Dias' (two caravels of about 50 tons each plus a supply ship).

items.bewering: Niemand in Europa het geweet of daar regtig 'n pad om Afrika was nie.
items.blok: Dias vaar suid met 'n klein vloot
items.bron: Ptolemy's Geography, still influential in the 15th century, made the Indian Ocean landlocked (Africa joined to a southern landmass). Fra Mauro's map (1459) THEORISED that Africa could be sailed around, but no voyage had confirmed it (Rare Maps essay 'The cartography of Africa to ca. 1570'; everything-everywhere.com on the Fra Mauro map). Encyclopedia.com: the Portuguese thought 'perhaps it was possible to sail to the Indian Ocean around Africa'. 'Weet' is accurate: it was believed by some and denied by others, but known by nobody.

items.bewering: Dias het verder suid gevaar as waar Europese skepe al langs hierdie kus gekom het.
items.blok: Dias vaar suid met 'n klein vloot
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Bartolomeu Dias': Dias passed the furthest point reached by Diogo Cão by December 1487, reaching Walvis Bay (Golfo da Conceição) on 8 December 1487 and then going on beyond it. The qualifier 'langs hierdie kus' keeps the claim exact.

items.bewering: Mense het natuurlik lankal langs daardie kus gewoon en daar kos gesoek.
items.blok: Dias vaar suid met 'n klein vloot
items.bron: SAHO, 'Khoikhoi' (herders in southern Africa from about 2300 years before present; they also kept hunting and gathering); Maas 2020 pp. 21-22, quoting the 1497 Roteiro of da Gama's voyage: people at St Helena Bay gathering honey and eating seals, whales and plant roots.

items.bewering: Later was hulle ver van die kus af in die oop see. Van so ver af kon die bemanning die kus glad nie sien nie.
items.blok: Om die suidpunt sonder om dit te sien
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Bartolomeu Dias' (about 30 days on the open ocean, a broad arc away from land); SAHO 'Bartolomeu Dias' ('Beating on for some days without sighting land'); A.E. Axelson, 'Popular fallacies about the Dias voyage 1487-1488', Historia (University of Pretoria) pp. 74-75 (deliberate long tacks out to sea). Whether a storm drove them out or they chose to go is debated (Axelson against Barros's storm). The lesson states no cause, which is correct.

items.bewering: Toe hulle weer land sien, was hulle al om die suidpunt van Afrika. Hulle het die suidpunt verbygevaar sonder om dit te sien.
items.blok: Om die suidpunt sonder om dit te sien
items.bron: SAHO 'Bartolomeu Dias' ('they unwittingly rounded the Cape of Good Hope in late January 1488'); Wikipedia 'Bartolomeu Dias' (the first landfall after the open-sea arc was the later Mossel Bay). Cape Agulhas and the Cape of Good Hope both lie west of Mossel Bay, so the claim holds whichever cape is meant.

items.bewering: Die skepe het in 1488 anker gegooi in die baai wat ons vandag Mosselbaai noem.
items.blok: Die skepe gooi anker by Mosselbaai
items.bron: Axelson, Historia p. 74 ('Dias' arrival, on 3 February 1488, at the Angra de Sao Bras, the later Mossel Bay'); SAHO 'Bartolomeu Dias' (early February 1488, Golfo de São Bras = Mossel Bay); Wikipedia 'Mossel Bay' (3 February 1488).

items.bewering: Die bemanning het aan wal gegaan om vars water in te neem.
items.blok: Die skepe gooi anker by Mosselbaai
items.bron: SAHO 'Bartolomeu Dias' (anchored 'to replenish water'); Bartolomeu Dias Museum Complex, 'Fountain' page (the crew filled their water containers at the freshwater spring; Pêro d'Alenquer recorded that Dias took water from a well near the beach).

items.bewering: Op die land by die baai was die Khoikhoi met hulle beeste.
items.blok: Die skepe gooi anker by Mosselbaai
items.bron: Bartolomeu Dias Museum, 'Fountain' page ('The local Khoekhoen, possibly Gouriqua ... drove their cattle and sheep inland when the Portuguese landed'); Barros, as translated in Maas 2020 p. 16 ('the many cows seen there, watched by their herdsmen').

items.bewering: Dias het vir hulle geskenke aangebied, maar hulle het weggevlug sonder om iets daarvan te vat.
items.blok: Die skepe gooi anker by Mosselbaai
items.bron: Roteiro of da Gama's first voyage, Ravenstein translation (Hakluyt Society 1898; Project Gutenberg #46440), at the Bay of São Braz: 'when Bartholomeu Dias was here the natives fled without taking any of the objects which he offered them.' SAHO's Dias page says instead that the Khoikhoi 'traded cattle and sheep' with Dias. That contradicts the primary source, the Dias Museum ('no bartering took place') and Maas p. 21 (da Gama was 'the first to barter with the Khoi'), so SAHO appears to have conflated the visits of 1488 and 1497. The lesson follows the primary source.

items.bewering: Dit is die eerste ontmoeting aan hierdie kus waarvan ons 'n opgetekende verslag het.
items.blok: Die skepe gooi anker by Mosselbaai
items.bron: Africultures, 'Des rencontres mémorables' (the first contact with the people of the south coast is recounted by a single text, written nine years later); Maas 2020 p. 17 (Dias brought home knowledge of people 'whom Europeans had never contacted before'); Axelson, Historia p. 74 (3 February 1488 was the first landfall after rounding). Dias made earlier stops on the Namibian west coast, so the qualifier 'aan hierdie kus' is load-bearing and must stay.

items.bewering: Twee Portugese verslae van later vertel van daardie dag.
items.blok: Die skepe gooi anker by Mosselbaai
items.bron: Axelson (Historia p. 74) names the only two narrative sources: João de Barros's Décadas da Ásia (1552) and the anonymous Roteiro of da Gama's 1497 voyage. Only the Roteiro clearly describes what happened at São Brás (Mossel Bay). Africultures likewise says the first south-coast contact is told by ONE text. Barros describes herders driving their cattle inland at 'Angra dos Vaqueiros'. Raper (Unisa, Portuguese place names) and Maas (2020, n. 3) identify that bay with Mossel Bay only 'probably'. Axelson, by contrast, writes that 'Barros failed to mention Dias' arrival, on 3 February 1488, at the Angra de Sao Bras', and cowherd names also attach to neighbouring places (Rio dos Vaqueiros = Gouritz River; Angra das Vaccas = Vleesbaai, SAHO place records). So whether Barros's account is about this bay at all is disputed. Separately, the Roteiro tells the flight and the watering incident as separate occasions ('Nay, on one occasion...'), so 'daardie dag' (one day) is not supported either. A person must decide: accept the claim, or narrow it to what holds whatever Barros meant, e.g. that most of what we know comes from one Portuguese account written about nine years later, with 'dag' replaced by 'besoek'.

items.bewering: Daar is geen opgeskrewe weergawe van die Khoikhoi se kant nie.
items.blok: Die skepe gooi anker by Mosselbaai
items.bron: Axelson, Historia p. 74 (the only sources are Barros and the Roteiro, both Portuguese); Maas 2020 ch. 1 (every pre-1652 account of the Khoi is European).

items.bewering: Die Khoikhoi het lankal daar gewoon en presies geweet waar die vars water is.
items.blok: Vir die Khoikhoi was dit hulle eie land
items.bron: SAHO 'Khoikhoi' (herding from about 2300 BP; herds moved for water and grazing; groups split over 'water and grazing rights'); Roteiro, Ravenstein 1898 (the people guarded the watering place at São Braz).

items.bewering: Hulle was veeboere met beeste en skape wat weiding en water nodig gehad het.
items.blok: Vir die Khoikhoi was dit hulle eie land
items.bron: SAHO 'Khoikhoi' (they kept goats, cattle and sheep and moved with the seasons to find grazing); Dias Museum (the Khoekhoen at Mossel Bay had cattle and sheep).

items.bewering: Hulle het in hul eie gemeenskappe gewoon, elk met eie leiers en eie reëls.
items.blok: Vir die Khoikhoi was dit hulle eie land
items.bron: SAHO 'Khoikhoi' (groups were led by chiefs, and a group that split off usually took its leader's name); Wikipedia 'Khoekhoe' (society organised into clans).

items.bewering: Nou het vreemdelinge met wapens aan wal gekom om by hulle water uit te kom. Die Khoikhoi moes self besluit wat hulle met daardie vreemdelinge gaan doen.
items.blok: Vir die Khoikhoi was dit hulle eie land
items.bron: Roteiro, Ravenstein 1898 (Dias came ashore for water and was armed with a crossbow; the people first fled and later resisted, so they acted on their own decisions); Dias Museum (the Portuguese came for the spring).

items.bewering: Die bemanning was al maande lank op see toe hulle by hierdie baai kom.
items.blok: Vir die Portugese was dit 'n vreemde kus
items.bron: SAHO 'Bartolomeu Dias' (left the Tagus in August 1487); Wikipedia (July or August 1487); arrived at Mossel Bay on 3/4 February 1488, so about six months at sea.

items.bewering: Hulle vars water was min en hulle het nuwe water nodig gehad.
items.blok: Vir die Portugese was dit 'n vreemde kus
items.bron: Maas 2020 p. 16 (Dias was 'dangerously low on supplies'); SAHO 'Bartolomeu Dias' (anchored to replenish water); the name Aguada de São Brás means 'watering place of St Blaise' (Wikipedia 'Mossel Bay').

items.bewering: Hulle het geen kaart van hierdie kus gehad nie. Hulle het ook nie geweet wie hier woon of wat die reëls is nie.
items.blok: Vir die Portugese was dit 'n vreemde kus
items.bron: No European had sailed this coast before (Wikipedia/SAHO 'Bartolomeu Dias'). Axelson p. 75: Dias himself charted the coast he discovered 'league by league'. Maas p. 17: the people there had never been contacted by Europeans.

items.bewering: Die twee kante kon nie mekaar se taal praat nie. Daar was ook geen tolk wat kon help nie.
items.blok: Hoekom dit verkeerd geloop het
items.bron: Barros, as translated in Maas 2020 p. 16 ('since they had no language which could be understood, we could have no speech with them'); Dias Museum ('Communication ... would be near impossible').

items.bewering: Dias was aan wal besig om vars water in te neem. Die Khoikhoi het hom probeer keer
items.blok: Hoekom dit verkeerd geloop het
items.bron: Roteiro, Ravenstein 1898: 'when Dias was taking in water, close to the beach, they sought to prevent him'.

items.bewering: want dit was hulle water.
items.blok: Hoekom dit verkeerd geloop het
items.bron: The primary source, the Roteiro, records only that they 'sought to prevent him'. It gives no reason. The Dias Museum interprets the event as the Portuguese filling their containers 'without permission from the Khoekhoen in whose territory they were', and SAHO's Khoikhoi page shows water rights mattered to Khoikhoi groups, so this is the best-supported reading. But SAHO's Dias page puts the killing down to 'lack of understanding', and other summaries say it is not clear what set the clash off. The lesson itself says, three blocks earlier, that there is no Khoikhoi account, then states their motive as fact. A person should decide whether to accept it or mark it as the likely reason (e.g. 'waarskynlik omdat ...').

items.bewering: Hulle het van 'n heuwel af klippe na hom gegooi. Dias het met 'n kruisboog geskiet en een van hulle doodgemaak.
items.blok: Hoekom dit verkeerd geloop het
items.bron: Roteiro, Ravenstein 1898: 'when they pelted him with stones, from a hill, he killed one of them with the arrow of a cross-bow'; SAHO 'Bartolomeu Dias' ('Snatching up a crossbow, Dias shot one of them dead'); Dias Museum.

items.bewering: Net een van die twee Portugese verslae vertel van hierdie dood.
items.blok: Hoekom dit verkeerd geloop het
items.bron: The Roteiro (Ravenstein 1898) records the killing. Barros's account, as quoted by Maas 2020 pp. 16-17 and summarised by Axelson, mentions herders who fled and no killing. This holds whatever the outcome of the 'twee verslae' item above, because the two surviving accounts are these two either way.

items.bewering: Dias het nog 'n end ver teen die suidooskus van Afrika opgevaar.
items.blok: Hoekom Dias omgedraai het
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Bartolomeu Dias' (padrão at Kwaaihoek near the Boesmans River mouth, 12 March 1488); SAHO 'Bartolomeu Dias' (on to Algoa Bay and a river probably the Keiskamma, the likely turning point).

items.bewering: Sy bemanning was toe al baie lank op see en heeltemal uitgeput. Die manne wou huis toe en Dias het omgedraai voordat hy die Ooste bereik.
items.blok: Hoekom Dias omgedraai het
items.bron: SAHO 'Bartolomeu Dias' (the men 'compelled him to return them to Portugal because they were exhausted and frightened and their provisions were running out'); Wikipedia (the officers unanimously favoured returning; Dias agreed).

items.bewering: Op die pad terug het hulle die suidpunt van Afrika wel gesien.
items.blok: Hoekom Dias omgedraai het
items.bron: SAHO 'Bartolomeu Dias' ('They saw Cape Agulhas on 16 May, but were unaware that this unimpressive point was the southern extremity of Africa'); SANParks notice on the Agulhas National Park Southern Tip Day; Wikipedia (the Cape of Good Hope was also first sighted on the return, in May 1488). 'Suidpunt' is correct for Cape Agulhas. If this ever gets narrowed, keep it Agulhas, because the Cape of Good Hope is not the southern tip.

items.bewering: Europese skepe het nou geweet 'n skip kan om die suidpunt van Afrika kom. Aan die ander kant kon 'n skip verder na die Ooste vaar. Dias se reis het gewys dat Portugal se plan werklik kon werk.
items.blok: Wat die reis vir Europa beteken het
items.bron: Axelson, Historia p. 76 ('By rounding the southern extremity of Africa and entering into the Indian Ocean the Dias expedition proved the practicality of a sea route from Europe to the Indies'); Encyclopedia.com 'Long-Distance Trade' (Dias's 1488 voyage showed that 'a sea route to the Indies was possible').

items.bewering: Die volgende Portugese vloot kon daarom verder as Dias probeer vaar.
items.blok: Wat die reis vir Europa beteken het
items.bron: Maas 2020 p. 21 (da Gama's voyage about ten years later reached India); Axelson p. 76 (Dias contributed directly to the da Gama expedition).

items.bewering: bemanning: Al die mense wat saam op een skip werk en vaar.
items.blok: begrip: bemanning
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'crew' ('all the people working on a ship, plane, etc.').

items.bewering: Khoikhoi: Veeboere met beeste en skape wat in Suider-Afrika gewoon het.
items.blok: begrip: Khoikhoi
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Khoekhoe' (present tense: 'the traditionally nomadic pastoralist indigenous population of Southern Africa'; current Khoekhoe groups include the Nama of Namibia, Botswana and South Africa, the Griqua and the !Orana clans); SAHO 'Khoikhoi' (Nama is still spoken today by the Namaqua). The definition says nothing false about 1488. But a glossary entry is read on its own, and in the past tense ('gewoon het') it defines the Khoikhoi as a people who existed and no longer do. That is the 'extinct' misconception about South Africa's Khoikhoi, and the sources contradict it.
items.regstelling: Define the Khoikhoi as a people who still live in Southern Africa, not as a people of the past. Their long history of herding stays, but must not be written in the present tense as if all Khoikhoi still herd. For example: 'Mense wat al baie lank in Suider-Afrika woon en van ouds af beeste en skape aanhou; Khoikhoi-groepe soos die Nama woon vandag nog hier.'

opsomming: The account of 1488 holds up against the primary source (the Roteiro of da Gama's voyage) and the Dias scholarship. The lesson has no analogies, and both superlatives are true as qualified. But two claims need a person: whether two Portuguese accounts really tell of 'that day' (Barros's 'Angra dos Vaqueiros' is only probably Mossel Bay, Axelson says Barros never mentions the São Brás landing, and the Roteiro does not put both events on one day), and the stated motive 'want dit was hulle water', which no source records. One fault the writer can fix: the Khoikhoi glossary entry is in the past tense and reads as if the Khoikhoi no longer exist.
